confidence_tier: B, PASS on both pre-registered falsifiers, one honest calibration caveat, one genuine refinement surfaced

pre_registration.C: a geometric F-V-curve derivation reproduces (i) monotone-decreasing peak bar velocity vs %1RM, (ii) an intermediate-load power optimum, (iii) proximal-to-distal joint sequencing, each vs a live-verified anchor
pre_registration.not_C: constant-velocity null NOT rejected (R^2<=0.50 everywhere) OR monotonic-power null NOT rejected (max at a tested extreme) OR sequencing ordering contradicted by a live source
pre_registration.forced_adversary: the task's own stated numeric bands could be self-flattering priors, not independent facts -- forced via live NCBI-eutils fetch of every citation, a dedicated hunt for elite-cohort success-vs-failure studies that could REFUTE the naive dysfunction framing, and re-deriving (not asserting) the model's quantitative 70pct1RM prediction

falsifiers.null_model: peak bar velocity is constant across %1RM
falsifiers.threshold: R^2 > 0.50 in a live-verified peer-reviewed load-velocity regression rejects the null

in_repo_recomputation.note: direction correct, not significant alone (n=3, one documented 75kg outlier already flagged upstream as real, not tracking artifact)

void_floor_control.purpose: a near-max attempt cluster must NOT be read as counter-evidence -- velocity bottoms at the minimal-velocity-threshold (MVT), not because load stops mattering

falsifiers.caveat: the 6 literature R^2 rows are squat/bench/bench-pull, NOT snatch/clean specifically -- no live-verified snatch/clean load-velocity regression table was found this session; the weightlifting-specific direction check is carried by the in-repo recomputation instead

falsifiers.null_model: mean/peak power rises or falls monotonically across the full tested load range (max at a tested extreme)

evidence.quote: Peak power was maximized at 70% 1RM, which was, however, not significantly different from peak power at 50, 60, 80, and 90% 1RM

geometric_derivation.model: Hill hyperbolic F-V curve, normalized F0=v0=1, curvature k=a/F0, F(v)=k(1+k)/(v+k)-k

claim_B_interior_power_max.textbook_cross_check: matches standard muscle-physiology 'peak power near 30% Vmax/Fmax' (qualitative, not a session citation)

geometric_derivation.ballistic_vs_grinding_subtlety: grinding lifts (squat/bench/deadlift): v(1RM)->0, interior power max is topologically FREE. Ballistic lifts (snatch/clean): v(1RM)=MVT>0, interior max within [0,1RM] is an EMPIRICAL question, not automatic -- this is why Kawamori/Kipp needed to measure it.

calibration_honesty.method: back-solve MVT/v0 so the model's predicted %1RM-at-power-optimum equals Kawamori's measured 70%, at k=0.25
calibration_honesty.status: CALIBRATED-CONSISTENT, NOT an independent a-priori prediction -- v0 is not independently measured anywhere in this cert or its cited literature; disclosed as a limitation, not hidden

joint_power_sequencing.ordering_claim: hip and knee extend significantly faster than ankle, independent of load (Kipp 2011, PMID 21240030)
joint_power_sequencing.torque_claim: hip and ankle produce significantly higher torques than knee (Kipp 2011) -- a DIFFERENT ordering axis than velocity, reported as measured, not merged into one ranking
joint_power_sequencing.timing_claim: the more successful/experienced lifter produces the larger positive-acceleration phase FIRST (Enoka 1979, PMID 491869)
joint_power_sequencing.skill_claim: skill differences show up in temporal organization of power phases, not peak power magnitude (Enoka 1988, PMID 3367754)
joint_power_sequencing.cross_cert_consistency_note: docs/MECHANISM_PUSHOFF_PLANTARFLEXOR.md (different movement, gait push-off) independently found ankle plantarflexor peak ~8%GC AFTER knee/hip peak -- qualitative consistency only, not pooled as evidence
joint_power_sequencing.honest_gap: no live-verified source gives an exact %-of-total-work-or-power breakdown per joint; searched 'energy contribution hip knee ankle weightlifting pull joint work' on PubMed, 0 hits

failed_lift_mechanism.task_framing: a failed/missed lift = insufficient bar velocity or height
failed_lift_mechanism.verdict: PARTIALLY REFUTED for the technical-near-miss regime; HOLDS for the load-capacity-limited regime

adversary_1.design: same athlete, same load, success vs failure
adversary_1.finding: no significant difference (p>0.05) in vertical bar velocity, trajectory, work, or power; differentiator was force-DIRECTION

adversary_2.design: world-class, same load, success vs frontward-drop
adversary_2.finding: no significant difference in maximum barbell height; differentiators were backward velocity/COM displacement (horizontal control)

failed_lift_mechanism.resolution: insufficient-velocity/height mechanism holds when attempting a load at/beyond current 1RM (no paired success exists); refuted for near-misses at a load the athlete otherwise makes, where direction/technical control dominates
